findings.issue: Actions string equality is case-insensitive, so github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' also admits a distinct MAIN/Main branch if dispatched. The same new guard in refresh-watchdog.yml:18 and update-and-deploy.yml:190 permits unchecked branch code or notifications to reach privileged steps; the existing operating-state entry has the same gap. tests/release-dispatch-ref-boundary.test.ts:40 incorrectly models Actions equality with case-sensitive JavaScript comparison. Require a case-sensitive runner ref check before checkout, source-secret use, watchdog dispatch and notification steps. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/expressions#operators

summary: Found and fixed one high-risk ref-admission defect: Actions compares strings case-insensitively, allowing a dispatched MAIN/Main branch through the new main guards. Added four first-step Bash checks before checkout, provider-secret use, dispatch or notification, corrected the offline comparison semantics, and observed four regression failures before the fix. Git Bash verification passes 1008 Vitest tests plus 5 Python tests, typecheck/build and operating-state checks; live Actions/Preview execution remains unverified, and no push or deployment was performed.
